title: Netanyahu accused of smearing Arab voters to hold on to power
author: Julian Borger in Jerusalem
text:
Prime minister claims Arab Israeli parties used foreign backing to steal elections, in which his coalition lost its majority

Benjamin Netanyahu has been accused of using smear tactics to cling to power, after he claimed that Arab Israeli parties had used foreign backing to “steal” Tuesday’s election, in which the prime minister’s coalition lost its parliamentary majority.

Netanyahu and his allies called on the internal security service, Shin Bet, to investigate alleged vote buying and other irregularities in Palestinian communities in Israel , supposedly funded by foreign money.

Gadi Eisenkot, the leader of the main opposition bloc, accused the prime minister and his Likud party of trying to derail the election results.

“It’s already clear that Likud and Netanyahu have embarked on a coordinated, organised campaign seeking to delegitimise the results of the election,” Eisenkot said in a video message.

The prime minister’s allegations were quickly disowned by a range of government officials, including police officers and members of the election committee. Netanyahu was also rebuked by the president for “tarnishing an entire community”.

On Wednesday night, the prime minister posted a statement by Likud online , which described the claimed violations as “an attack on democracy whose purpose is to lead to a foreign takeover of the Knesset, the Islamisation of Israel, and the overthrow of rightwing rule”.

Tuesday’s elections led to Netanyahu’s far-right coalition losing its majority after four years in power. The main Jewish opposition bloc also fell short, however, leaving two Arab Israeli parties, the Joint List and Ra’am, holding the balance of power .

The prime minister’s attack appeared aimed at stopping the Jewish and Arab opposition voting together in the new Knesset to oust the incumbent speaker, Amir Ohana, a Likud politician and former Shin Bet official, and advancing their own legislation.

The Likud statement posted by Netanyahu on X said: “It is clear that no Zionist party should cooperate with Ra’am and the Joint List, replace the Knesset speaker through votes bought for cash, and form a government that is dangerous to Israel.”

Opposition leaders lambasted the claims of Netanyahu, 77, who has run Israel for 19 of the past 30 years.

Yousef Jabareen, the Joint List leader, accused the prime minister of incitement. “Netanyahu was defeated at the ballot box,” Jabareen said, adding that he “refuses to come to terms with the fact that the Arab public voted and decided”.

Eisenkot said any investigation should be conducted “without fear or favour,” and with “the utmost caution”, but insisted it could not be used as a reason to delay the convening of the newly elected Knesset, due to be sworn in within 14 days of the election.

The acting director general of the central elections committee, Dean Livneh, said there appeared to be no basis for the claims. Police officials quoted across the Israeli press said the allegations were groundless, adding that voting had been relatively trouble-free.

The president, Isaac Herzog, called for political leaders to “avoid tarnishing an entire community that sought to exercise its right to vote and take an active part in democracy”.

It was not specified in Likud statements, but press reports said Qatar was the foreign power alleged to have funded vote-buying and voter mobilisation. Majed al-Ansari, an adviser to Qatar’s prime minister, said its government “categorically” denied any involvement in the elections.

With almost all the votes counted, Netanyahu’s coalition has 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset, Eisenkot’s bloc has 48, and the Joint List and Ra’am together have 19 seats, a historic high for the Arab Israeli community, which makes up about a fifth of Israel’s population.

The record turnout among Arab Israelis (Palestinians with Israeli citizenship) appeared to be driven by outrage at routine discrimination and fear that it could become far worse if extremist and openly racist members of the government, such as the national security minister, Itamar Ben-Gvir, and the finance minister, Bezalel Smotrich, secured another term in office.

On Thursday, Ben-Gvir called for the arrest of Arab party leaders, and Smotrich demanded they be subjected to Shin Bet interrogation.

Voting in Nazareth, the biggest majority-Palestinian town in Israel, was brisk on Tuesday, with few signs of irregularities, other than apparent ploys by the government and coalition parties to suppress the Arab vote.

Some packets of ballots sent to Nazareth polling stations were in Hebrew alone, rather than in Hebrew and Arabic. Election workers said that monitors sent by far-right parties had attempted procedural ploys to slow down voting but had been largely unsuccessful.

The leaders of the Joint List and the Zionist “Change” bloc have ruled out a formal coalition, but officials from both have discussed the possibility of tactical voting in the Knesset to unseat Ohana, the speaker, and to pass some consensus legislation.

One proposed bill would establish a commission of inquiry into the security failures that helped lead to the Hamas attack on Israel on 7 October 2023, something Netanyahu has blocked over the past two years.

Ahmad Tibi, a party leader on the Joint List, said Netanyahu was trying to subvert the election results by trying to sabotage a common front between the Eisenkot bloc and the Arab Israeli parties.

“This entire campaign is directed against Eisenkot, to prevent him, intimidate and scare him off forming a government that relies on external support from the Joint List or Ra’am,” Tibi told the Reuters news agency.

Naftali Bennett, a former prime minister who is a partner in the “Change” bloc, pointed out the irony of Netanyahu denouncing Qatar for election meddling while the Israeli leader’s own political advisers are being accused of taking Qatari money for promoting the Gulf monarchy’s image.…

title: Reddit is moving to “a logged-in-only experience,” CEO says
author: Scharon Harding
text:
In the future, you won’t be able to use Reddit without logging in.

Reddit CEO Steve Huffman confirmed the impending change in a letter (PDF) to shareholders today about Q3 performance. He said that Reddit is shifting “to a logged-in-only experience," adding:

Moving to primarily logged-in will ensure our users have the best Reddit experience possible, and can find the content and communities most relevant to them. It is better for our business because we will have more signals for ads targeting, and being logged-in leads to higher engagement generally. It also allows us to protect access to Reddit’s extremely valuable corpus of data, and helps us better adapt to emerging regulations around the world.

Huffman also said that the login requirement will help Reddit better retain new users.

title: Who can compete as a gravel pro in Unbound? Organisers of Life Time Grand Prix establish new 'Pro Number' qualification process
author: jackie.tyson@futurenet.com (Jackie Tyson)
text:
A 'LT Pro Number' will now be required for riders to compete in the professional category across Life Time events, from the Sea Otter Qualifier in April to individual events that are part of the Life Time Grand Prix off-road series, including Unbound Gravel 200.

Many athletes will receive automatic approval for a LT Pro Number, based on past results in Life Time pro events, the Life Time Grand Prix series, as well as status with national and world championships, related to mountain bike or gravel.

Life Time, which owns and operates more than 195 athletic country clubs across the U.S. and Canada as well as endurance, cycling and running events, also outlined factors considered by a selection committee which will look at results in age groups and races outside the Life Time family.

Safety was the driving factor to implement the new criteria, based on results as well as past experience. The process was also seen as a way to "further professionalize the sport", as the Life Time Grand Prix enters a sixth season in 2027.

“We love that our events bring together athletes of all ages and abilities, and create opportunities for people to challenge themselves. At the same time, mass participant events like Unbound and Leadville are fast and can be tightly packed, particularly at the front of the field.

"Establishing clear, performance-based criteria for the Pro start helps ensure riders competing at the front have demonstrated the experience and ability to race safely at that level, while providing a transparent pathway for athletes to earn their place," Michelle Duffy, director of the Life Time Grand Prix, stated in the announcement on Thursday.

Concerns about the scramble for positioning at the front of the elite fields had been raised in the past by athletes themselves, especially at the two most demanding races - Unbound Gravel 200 and Leadville Trail 100 MTB.

During the Unbound Gravel 200 two years ago, there were several crashes involving less-experienced riders with Grand Prix contenders in the first six miles. The new protocols will help ensure riders have "demonstrated the ability and experience to compete at the front of the fast-race starts" before they line up, according to Life Time.

This new vetting system requires each rider to register online, with one approval covering all events for one year. The LT Pro Number does not guarantee entry, with registration or lottery request still required.

For LT Pro Qualifier races, such as Sea Otter Classic Gravel 60, Sea Otter Classic Fuego XL, Lutsen 99er and four other events, the races are open to all participants and no LT Pro Number is required. With good results, a rider can earn an LT Pro Number in order to complete registration for LT Pro events.

Life Time noted that the entire process would be transparent, with all cut off times and qualifying places posted publicly for athletes to track.

title: Alonso doubles down on poor F1 driving standards – and says those targeted know who they are
Life Time Unveils Standardized Qualification Requirements for Its Pro Races
author: Will Tracy
text:
Life Time has unveiled standardized qualifying criteria for riders looking to enter the pro category at Unbound Gravel, Leadville, and its other marquee races.

For 2027, riders wishing to race in the pro fields will need to obtain an “LT Pro Number”. Some riders will qualify automatically based on their previous results in Life Time events. Others will need to submit an application with proof that they meet other standards, listed below.

Riders only need to qualify once per season and are good to go for the remaining races in the calendar year once they qualify. Receiving an LT Pro Number is not a race entry or guarantee of a spot at a race; it only allows a rider to enter the pro race. Riders still need to sign up for each race. It is also not an entry into the Life Time Grand Prix; rather, it allows racers to enter the pro field at those events.

An LT Pro number will be needed to enter the pro field in the seven races that also comprise the Life Time Grand Prix. The Sea Otter Classic Gravel Pro Race, Unbound Gravel 200, Leadville Trail 100 MTB, Chequamegon MTB Festival, Little Sugar MTB, Big Sugar Gravel, and The Rad Dirt Fest all require an LT Pro number for the pro race.

The announcement is Life Time’s latest change aimed at creating more standardized, transparent pro racing qualification. Life Time announced this summer standardized qualification criteria for making the 25-rider fields for the Life Time Grand Prix , the premier offroad racing series in North America.

As gravel racing has become more competitive and faster over the years, Life Time has taken steps in the name of safety, including moving the pros to their own start times ahead of the mass participation rides. Now, Life Time is hoping that standardized criteria will make the pro races safer by limiting spots to top riders.

“We love that our events bring together athletes of all ages and abilities, and create opportunities for people to challenge themselves,” said Michelle Duffy, director of the Life Time Grand Prix. “At the same time, mass participant events like Unbound and Leadville are fast and can be tightly packed, particularly at the front of the field. Establishing clear, performance-based criteria for the Pro start helps ensure riders competing at the front have demonstrated the experience and ability to race safely at that level, while providing a transparent pathway for athletes to earn their place.”

Being fast doesn’t necessarily go hand in hand with being a safe racer, but the new criteria should help limit the pro fields to more experienced riders.

There are a number of pathways to qualify for Pro status at Life Time races.

Several criteria qualify riders automatically for an LT Pro Number. 2025 and 2026 results both count for 2027.

Life Time has denoted seven races as LT Pro Qualifiers, where a top result can earn you an LT Pro Number. The key word here is can, because you need to finish top-three and within 10% of the winner’s time.

Cutoff times for both LT Pro and LT Pro Qualifiers can be found here .

Racers can also earn an LT Pro number through these alternate pathways, though these will be reviewed by a committee and are not automatic. The committee is made up of Life Time race and series staff.

There are 19 non-Life Time events that offer racers a chance to qualify for an LT Pro Number.

In addition to qualifying with finish time, or a combination of overall position and finish time, racers who win their age group overall in a Life Time qualifying race can also apply for an LT Pro Number. Racers with an LT Pro number are not required to race pro and can opt to race age group instead.

You can read more about qualification and apply here . Applying is free and racers are allowed to reapply with every qualifying result they earn. Qualification is good for that calendar year, after which racers will need to either reapply or qualify automatically for 2028 based on 2027 results. You will hear back from the committee within a week.

title: JD Vance letter may offer last chance to avert fresh conflict between US and Iran
author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
text:
US vice-president writes to top Iranian security official in sign Washington has not abandoned diplomacy

Hopes of averting a major new conflagration between Iran and the US soon after Tuesday’s midterm elections could rest on Iran’s response to a personal letter from the US vice-president, JD Vance , offering to restart diplomacy.

The letter, written after predominantly Qatari mediation, was sent to the secretary of Iran’s supreme national security council, Mohsen Rezaei on Sunday. It requires Tehran to agree to make commitments on its nuclear programme at the start of a process that would lead to the opening of the strait of Hormuz within seven days in return for US sanctions relief.

A reply is imminent, but Iran is reluctant to give upfront and irreversible commitments on its nuclear programme, such as exporting its stockpile of highly enriched uranium to a third country, if the compensatory US steps, such as lifting sanctions on Iranian oil exports, are reversible.

Some form of third-party guarantee that both sides will adhere to their commitments has been discussed, with China often mentioned as the only country of sufficient status to underwrite it.

The return of Vance, a sceptic about the war, to the negotiations is significant and a sign the US has not abandoned diplomacy.

One Democratic senator briefed on the targets the US military had identified in Iran said the plan for a renewed attack was “insane” and would lead to “the likely destruction of our commitment to the rule of law”.

In a sign of Iran’s reluctance to meet US demands about sequencing, its chief negotiator, Mohammad Ghalibaf, wrote on X: “Iran’s conditions have been repeatedly and clearly stated to the mediators. The carrot-and-stick approach has no effect on Iran. Progress can only be achieved once Iran’s seven conditions have been agreed upon.”

Those conditions include lifting sanctions, ending asset freezes and ending the war on all fronts, a phrase that requires an Israeli ceasefire in Lebanon.

The US wants front-loaded, specific commitments about the removal of Iran’s stockpile of highly enriched uranium. Tehran is reluctant to give up its bargaining leverage, and is also resistant to the return of UN nuclear inspectors for fear they might provide the US with intelligence on the whereabouts and state of the stockpile.

It has proposed blending the stockpile down so it is no longer usable to make a nuclear weapon.

The Vance letter was sent to Rezaei rather than Ghalibaf or the foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, because Washington judged that decision-making power rests with those closest to the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps. In practice, Iran tries to reach decisions through consensus at the highest level of government in a six strong committee.

Ghalibaf and Rezaei met the supreme leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, last week to discuss the risk of a new war. Khamenei has said he would like an end to the current state of neither war nor peace. Iran has well-laid plans ready to strike back against US interests in the region, by hitting desalination plants, internet cables and electricity grids across the Gulf.

For a third US attack in two years to have any rationale, or prospect of inducing Iran’s capitulation, the plan would require the US, probably in conjunction with a caretaker government in Israel, to mount attacks on previously off-limits targets. Europe would not join the attacks, but the views of the Gulf states, the chief targets of Iran reprisals, would be key.

The Connecticut senator Chris Murphy told a briefing at the Middle East Institute: “I did get a fairly detailed conversation about what the war plan would be … I will just say this their plan is insane. It will lead to devastating escalation and the likely destruction of our commitment to the rule of law.

“There has been open reporting as to the civilian infrastructure we may be targeting … I think the plan they have developed will lead, in my judgment, to a prolongment [sic] and escalation of this war that will be devastating to our security interest.”

Although Tehran trusts Vance marginally more than most White House politicians and envoys, the Iranian high command is still suspicious about his status after he negotiated a 14-point memorandum of understanding which then fell apart when other members of the US administration took charge of its implementation.

That led to unilateral US steps to reopen the strait of Hormuz that Iran said contravened the terms of the agreement. Trump also came to detest it because it delayed the start of nuclear talks for as long as 60 days.

In an offer made by Tehran on the margins of the UN general assembly recently, it proposed foreshortening the timeframe before nuclear talks started, saying they could start withinsix or seven days of the US restoring the sanctions waiver on its oil exports and the reopening of the strait of Hormuz.

title: Burnham 'ready to support' Poundland staff as retailer faces collapse
text:
The future of Poundland hangs in the balance as the discount chain edges towards collapse.

The retailer's bosses have filed a notice of intention to appoint administrators which will give the business 10 days breathing space to find a rescue deal.

The move comes after Poundland's managing director Barry Williams wrote a memo to his 12,000 staff saying the chain's US owner had limited Poundland's access to funding despite strong sales.

It is understood the firm's owner, Gordon Brothers, wants to break up the firm, with rivals Poundstretcher, B&M and Lidl interested in potentially buying up stores.

Gordon Brothers bought Poundland, which had been struggling, from the Polish retail group Pepco in June last year for a nominal £1, but a little over a year later it put the business up for sale.

Irish firm Martin Property Group (MPG) put forward a bid to take the business on as a going concern, which was the preferred option for management, but it is understood this did not meet Gordon Brothers' expectations.

Gordon Brothers wants to recoup a £30m shareholder loan it inherited from the previous owners as part of a its deal, but it is understood the Martin Property Group offer was for £5m, with the rest of the payment deferred.

It means Poundland is now heading towards an insolvency process.

Gordon Brothers could secure a new owner through what is known as a pre-pack administration.

But the most likely option is for the business to be broken up and for parcels of stores to be sold.

Poundland was founded in 1990 with a store in Burton-upon-Trent, and has around 20 million customers per year.

It has across its 600 stores in the UK and Ireland, where it trades as Dealz.

It sells low-cost everyday products, general merchandise and fashion on local high streets.

Business secretary Jonathan Reynolds said the government was "keeping a close eye" the future of Poundland thought said the government had "no standing role" in the process.

"This is a business that has been turned around, it employs thousands of people," he told the BBC.

"If there is a potential owner that can continue that progress, obviously that naturally sounds like the best way forward so if that hasn't been accepted I want to know why that is the case."

The curious case of why Poundland is struggling during a cost-of-living crisis

Poundland in rescue talks as owners seek buyer

A Gordon Brothers insider said breaking the firm up would allow creditors to recover more money, and that this process would ultimately offer the best outcome for staff. The US investment firm's position is that current employees may be able to get employment with new store owners.

If this type of insolvency happens, it would let interested parties firm up offers.

These include Poundstretcher owner, Fortress, which according to one insider is interested in taking on between 200 and 250 stores.

Another large retailer is understood to be interested in buying up more than 100 other sites.

More than half a dozen retailers, include Iceland, Lidl, and B&M, have expressed interest in Poundland's store estate.

Bally Auluk, a national officer at the Usdaw shopworkers union, said this week had been "incredibly distressing" for Poundland staff.

He claimed staffwere having to "watch from the sidelines as a multi-billion pound company jeopardises their livelihoods as it tries to extract £30m from a business it bought for £1".

He said Williams had "reluctantly" kicked off the administration process, to give the business time to find a rescue deal, adding that Usdaw was urging Gordon Brothers to reconsider.

There is also a split between the owners and the management running Poundland, who described the situation as "unexpected, unwanted and wholly avoidable".

"As you all know, our sales are strong and our recovery is taking root. This business simply does not deserve to go into any kind of administration," the chain's managing director Williams said in a message to staff this week.

He revealed that Gordon Brothers had limited Poundland's access to funds which help it run its day-to-day business.

"I'm disappointed to have to tell you that Gordon Brothers have given instructions that restricts our access to funds that we would, in normal circumstances expect to access fully under our existing loan agreement," he added.

In the memo, seen by the BBC, Williams said the offer from Martin Property Group was a "fully funded, ready to go bid that would have kept the business intact and able to continue the remarkable progress we've made".

Three independent directors who were appointed earlier this month to help oversee a sale resigned with immediate effect after disagreeing with Gordon Brothers' decision not to accept MPG's solvent offer.

Gordon Brothers has lined up AlixPartners as administrators.

title: Hong Kong’s leader apologises for residential fire that killed 168 people
author: Guardian reporter
text:
Blaze was world’s deadliest residential fire since 1980, but some survivors and bereaved families say justice has yet to be served

Hong Kong’s leader has apologised for government shortcomings that contributed to a fire that killed 168 people in the city last year, a rare sign of public contrition that nevertheless failed to impress some victims’ families.

The chief executive, John Lee, and seven other officials bowed in apology at the release of a report that pointed to “decades of failure” by government bodies.

Four departments “should bear part of the responsibility” for the high casualties, the report said. So far one official, housing secretary Winnie Ho, has resigned.

Last November, a small fire probably started by a cigarette grew into an inferno that enveloped seven of the eight towers in Wang Fuk Court, a housing complex that was shrouded in bamboo scaffolding and netting for renovations.

Former residents and victims’ families have been waiting to see how the government will address who is to blame for the ignored warnings, substandard building materials and disabled fire alarms that made the fire the world’s deadliest in a residential building since 1980.

Authorities have filed charges, including manslaughter, against seven individuals and two companies over their roles in the fire. At least 35 people have been arrested.

The independent report released on Thursday found the “main culprits” of the fire were private contractors but also accused officials of “lax enforcement”.

Had the four departments better recognised the risks and acted accordingly, “there was a real possibility that the misconduct of the private-sector parties and the fire hazards in WF Court could have been rectified or removed before the fire”, it said.

Lee said a three-month investigation would now begin into the government’s role.

“I am deeply saddened. I would like to apologise to the affected residents and the general public,” Lee said on Thursday, adding that housing minister Ho should “bear political responsibility”.

But Yip Ka-kui, who lost his wife and home in the fire, told reporters he did not consider the government’s acceptance of accountability adequate. “All the secretaries for the departments named should step down,” he said, according to AFP news agency. “Administrative responsibility falls short” and political accountability even more so, Yip added.

Phyllis Lo, whose mother died in the fire, told AP news agency that progress had been made but that justice had yet to be served.

She added the officials’ apology was late, though it was better than nothing.

Hong Kong’s government has previously been accused by critics of being more concerned with clamping down on criticism than addressing the causes of the disaster.

Since a national security law was imposed on the city in 2020 by Beijing, the city’s once vibrant civil society groups and political opposition have been all but quashed.

In the weeks after the fire, authorities warned against crimes that “exploit the tragedy” and reportedly arrested at least three people for sedition.

China’s national security agency in Hong Kong also summoned international media representatives, saying they had smeared the government in their reports on the fire.

On Thursday Lee promised that “similar incidents will never be allowed to happen again”.

Some observers had called for a more legally powerful inquiry commission to be set up, rather than the judge-led independent review committee that compiled Thursday’s report.

Lee told reporters that authorities had proposed “systematic reforms”, including criminalising bid-rigging and overhauling the complaints system.

The report stated: “The fire has been put out, but the reform has only just begun.”

title: The South West reacts to Budget announcements
text:
Tourism and hospitality leaders have been reacting to this week's Budget.

Among the headlines in chancellor John Healey's first Budget on Wednesday were a £100 payment to help millions of households with energy bills, a VAT cut on electricity bills and a freeze on fuel duty, both extended to July.

It also announced Devon would get an elected mayor in 2028 white Cornwall was included as the only area on a pathway to become a Foundation Strategic Authority.

Sue Jewell, chair of South East Cornwall Tourism Association and a holiday accommodation provider, said the budget "gave with one hand and took with the other".

As part of the Budget legal minimum wage is to rise by 3.9% in April

Jewell said: "I think it's tricky because actually I would believe that quite a lot of people in our business anyway pay over the minimum wage just to retain staff.

"However because of the cost we've cut back on staff.

"Which is sad really because it's local people who could be having local jobs."

Dr Harry Pitts, senior lecturer in Politics at the University of Exeter's Cornwall Campus, said the £100 energy payment was one of the "small things to make life a little easier for some households in the immediate period".

Anyone living in a home in council tax bands A to D in England, will receive a one-off £100 "Household Energy Payment", funded by extra tax on banks.

The Budget announced the threshold at which high street shops start paying business rates in England was to be increased from £12,000 to £18,000, meaning businesses would pay no rates on properties with a rateable value below this level.

Toby Parkins, interim ceo at the Cornwall Chamber of Commerce, said he predicted this would benefit about 900 extra businesses in Cornwall.

"For the small business that is a big win," he said.

Helen Wylde-Archibald, from the Devon Chamber of Commerce, said she "welcomed some stability".

"The last two have been a bit scary for business," she said, referring to previous Budgets.

She added: "It doesn't necessarily give us all the conditions we want for full growth and strong growth, but the main thing was there was no broad base business tax rises and fuel duty remains frozen until July."

She said she didn't think there was enough in the way of announcements of more support for farming and food, and this had "an impact on the rural economy".

James Kittow, from Butcher & Grazier in Cornwall, said: "It just seems like we've been forgotten again.

"We're an industry that is ready, willing and able to help the country produce the food for the nation."

He added there was no change on inheritance tax for farmers. Since April, inherited farming assets worth more than £2.5m face 20% inheritance tax

"I'm looking to plan for a succession... we want to keep farming, we want to keep doing what we love doing but if we're going to get hit on the other end of it then it does make you think twice about what is all this for, and it's just so sad for the future farmers that want to come into the trade," he said.

Andrea Drew, managing director at Lander Mortgage Services, said the key announcement relating to housing was a scheme for first time buyers, and a a "First Time Buyer Isa".

This is an account in which savers can build up a deposit, with the government topping up contributions of up to £4,000 each year with a 25% bonus.

"The only negative I would say... on new builds, the housing market isn't just all about new builds, it's about existing property... because not everybody wants to have a new build property," she said.

She added: "The other thing was about the increase in tax for landlords so, they're increasing the tax by 4%."

She said she'd seen landlords who decided to sell their property because of the amount of tax but tenants couldn't afford to buy the homes.

"What tenants need is more homes to choose from, not fewer, and they can't solve the housing shortage by destroying people who are providing the housing," she said.

title: Cuts like a knife: Canadian rocker Bryan Adams trolls Trump with new song
author: Leyland Cecco in Toronto
text:
Musician wrote a ‘love letter’ to Canada with a new album – and some pointed commentary about the US president

Lake Ontario, the vast body of water that straddles the US-Canada border, has gone by many names over the centuries: Lac Saint-Louis, Lacus Ontarius, Skaniadorio, Cataraqui Lake. But one thing it will never be called, says the Canadian rock star Bryan Adams , is Lake America.

In his new song Lake Ontario, Adams takes aim at the US president, Donald Trump , accusing him of “breaking the peace” between the people who live on the lake’s shores.

Trump signed an executive order in August directing US federal agencies to rename Lake Ontario “Lake America”, echoing his earlier, widely mocked decision to rename the Gulf of Mexico “the Gulf of America”.

The move further escalated a feud with Canada that has strained the longstanding alliance between the two countries. Trump’s decision has largely been met with derision in Canada, with some pointing out that the province of Ontario is named after the lake, not the other way around. Adams’s lyrics emphasise the roots of the name:

The ‘lake of shining waters ’ is what the Iroquois called her

It’s a First Nations name – not an executive order.

Adams’s lyrics also suggest that Trump’s naming stunt was intended to deflect from the president’s other political problems, including the war in Iran and renewed scrutiny of the Jeffrey Epstein files.

But things weren’t going his way in Iran

So like a baby tossing the toys from the pram

While the Epstein files were getting traction

The song is part of what Adams described in a recent interview as a broader “love letter” to Canada: a songwriting project that began with an invitation from a film company to write about the Maritimes provinces of Canada and has since morphed into the upcoming album How’s It Goin’.

“After finishing the first song, I moved on to that one, and then moved on to another one, and then started thinking maybe I should just carry on with my theme,” he said.

As well as homages to Canadian heroes , the album also includes 51st State, released on 1 July – Canada Day – as another repudiation of Trump, in this case his efforts to annex Canada.

The first time he played the song in public was in the US.

“We weren’t sure how people were going to respond to it,” he said. “But we got a standing ovation every night for it. It made me think: perhaps, finally, the tide’s turning.”

title: Brazil’s victory for the planet and democracy: seven lessons from Lula’s win
author: Jonathan Watts
text:
The trouncing of the far right provides a playbook for social and environmental movements in other countries facing elections, including the US, Spain and France

Thank you, Brazil , for demonstrating how the far right can be trounced while protection for the Amazon is strengthened. In a world where nature and democracy appeared to be bleeding out in tandem, voters and forest defenders in this global south powerhouse have shown it is possible to staunch the flow. This should provide much needed inspiration and, more practically, a playbook for social and environmental movements in other countries facing elections, including the US, Spain and France.

The astonishing comeback victory of Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in Sunday’s presidential runoff against his extreme right challenger Flavío Bolsonaro has brought oceans of rapturous supporters on to the streets, while also thrilling conservationists, climate activists and social justice campaigners across the world.

Coming just weeks after the Lula administration announced a record fall in Amazon and Cerrado destruction, they hope Brazil can now go on to achieve its target of zero deforestation by 2030 and continue to support a global transition away from fossil fuels. That would provide a huge boost to flagging global efforts to stabilise the climate and protect degraded ecosystems. It would also set a remarkable example of leadership by the global south.

Big battles lie ahead. In the Amazon region itself, far-right members of Bolsonaro’s party have won the governorships of seven of the nine states and a large number of municipal mayorships. Brazil’s congress is now dominated by agribusiness and mining interests that have set the political agenda in recent years, and will push hard to allow more extractivist industries in indigenous lands, expand road-building, privatise rivers, weaken environmental protections and possibly attempt to impeach the president.

In the regional sphere, Lula, alone among the leaders of main South American nations in not aligning with Donald Trump’s so-called Shield of the Americas, will face pressure from Washington to channel critical minerals and other natural resources to the US, rather than selling to China or Europe, or leaving them in the ground. And, on the planetary level, Brazil faces the threat of accelerating global heating, which is pushing the Amazon ever closer to the point of no return.

So although Sunday’s result will hopefully provide a little breathing space for the Amazon and other crucially important biomes, the joy and hope that Brazil has gifted the world will quickly fade unless it inspires political change in other countries. In that sense, the biggest environmental impact of Lula’s victory may be the lessons it provides for campaigners elsewhere. Here are some initial takeaways:

1 Politics matter . There is no higher environmental priority than defeating the far right, which is a Trojan horse for extractivist – and often criminal – groups to capture states and erode protections for people, democracy and the environment. Just look at the 59.5% surge of Amazon deforestation under the 2019-2022 term of Jair Bolsonaro – the highest level of any four-year presidency in Brazil. Compare that with the 71.2% fall during the Lula administration. Over the past year, forest loss was 3,335 sq km, the lowest level since the start of satellite measurements in 1988. And Lula is not, by any means, an environmentalist. He has approved several destructive projects himself, but he is a people person who listens to the voice of social movements.

2 Don’t give up . Lula was largely written off by the markets and some polls after his first-round defeat. No first-round loser had ever previously come back to win the runoff. Lula was able to do so by securing an extra 10m votes over three weeks. The energy for this came from the streets and the forests. Social movements organised giant rallies in cities. In the Amazon, indigenous, riverine and quilombola groups travelled by hours – sometimes days – to reach polling stations by boats or buses.

3 Mobilise a campaign army . The first round of Lula’s campaign had been stodgy, old-fashioned and defensive – three traits that are also often applicable to environmental campaigns. This was transformed during the runoff, when federal deputy André Janones launched a “Lula’s Army” WhatsApp group that used humorous memes, live streams and algorithmic outreach to seize digital territory that had long been dominated by the right. By voting day, this army had 10m “soldiers”, about 8% of the electorate. Volunteers devoted hours posting stories and spreading messages across social media, speeding up the Lula campaign’s response time and emotional impact. Everyone was instructed not to share or respond to posts by the opposition camp.

4 Go on the offensive against US tech giants. Lula’s campaign accused Meta, which runs the Facebook, WhatsApp and Instagram social media platforms, of political favouritism towards Bolsonaro in its algorithms and AI tools. Meta denied bias but acknowledged technical failures. Brazil’s electoral court ordered corrective action. Among the most popular chants of Lula supporters was “Hey Meta, vai tomar no cu!” (Hey Meta, take it up the arse!). Many on the left have blamed US social media platforms for spreading rightwing disinformation and fearmongering, causing recent electoral defeats in Colombia , Chile and Peru. Lula made clear that would not be allowed in Brazil: “We had to overcome foreign interference through digital platforms, which we will have to regulate. We cannot have a monstrously large corporation earning millions and billions paying no taxes to this country and trying to steer our election results.”…

title: Antonelli to miss Mexico media day with illness
text:
Kimi Antonelli is to miss Thursday's Mexico City Grand Prix media day with an illness as he stands on the brink of clinching his first world title.

The Italian's Mercedes team said that Antonelli had a "viral illness" and had been excused his duties on Thursday by governing body the FIA "as a precaution to give him the chance to rest ahead of the weekend".

A Mercedes spokesperson said: "We expect him to be back tomorrow."

Practice for the race starts on Friday at 18:30 GMT.

Antonelli will seal the championship, and become the youngest winner in Formula 1 history, as long as he does not lose more than two points to team-mate George Russell and one point to Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton in the grand prix on Sunday.

The only way he could be stopped from tying up the title is if one of Russell and Hamilton wins. Ninth would be enough for Antonelli to become champion if it is Russell, and 10th if it is Hamilton.

How to follow Mexico City Grand Prix on the BBC

Antonelli is one of two drivers to miss media day with an illness.

The other is Cadillac's Valtteri Bottas, who his team said was "unwell".

A Cadillac spokesperson said: "The team has taken the decision to allow him a day of rest, to support his recovery.

"This is a precautionary measure and does not currently affect his participation in the remainder of the race weekend. We will continue to monitor the situation and provide updates if necessary."

On Wednesday, Cadillac announced a new contract for the Finn's team-mate Sergio Perez, who will stay with the team until at least 2029.

They made no mention of Bottas' future in the announcement, and are said by insiders to be considering whether to promote their American reserve driver Colton Herta into F1.

Herta is having his fifth outing of the year in practice on Friday at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez, as the team seek to earn him enough mileage to secure the so-called super licence that is required to race in F1.

Herta, previously a front-runner in the US-based Indycar championship, moved to Formula 2 this year with the intention of preparing himself for F1.

His season has not gone well and he is currently 19th in the standings with a best result of fifth place.

However, Cadillac feel he has shown more potential in his F1 outings, which also include a number of runs in cars from previous years.

No decision has been made on whether Bottas or Herta will partner Perez in 2027.

title: Chelsea’s fine finishing has them flying high – but how long can it last?
author: Andrew Beasley
text:
Despite being at opposite ends of the table, according to Opta’s expected points model, Chelsea have performed worse than Saturday’s opponents Manchester United

M ichael Carrick will arrive at Stamford Bridge on Saturday with the air of a dead man walking. Yet despite Manchester United being fifth-bottom of the Premier League and Chelsea fifth-top, the Blues have performed worse this season according to Opta’s expected points model.

Is there a glitch in the matrix? Has the fabled supercomputer clicked on a suspicious link? Even though the margin between their data is small, it feels unthinkable that Chelsea could be below United’s level.

That is until you review a few statistics. Xabi Alonso’s side held healthy expected goal margins in their wins over Fulham, Brighton and Everton, but were heavily outgunned against Arsenal and Brentford. The xG count went slightly against them versus Hull, Bournemouth and Tottenham, which is concerning when all three were at home in matches they would reasonably expect to win.

Opta’s data suggests Chelsea are the 12th-best team in the Premier League . They have risen to fifth by virtue of a hot finishing streak. Chelsea have scored 6.7 goals more than the quality of their chances imply they deserve, second only to Brighton (6.8), or above them if penalties are excluded. Chelsea scored five times from 10 shots against Bournemouth; while not without precedent, managing so many goals from so few efforts happens less than once a season in the Premier League.

Jordan Henderson has scored twice from five shots outside the box, after finding the net once for every 20 long-range efforts he attempted between 2014 and last season. Pedro Neto’s total of three league goals is two shy of his career best for a Premier League campaign. Morgan Rogers outscoring his expected goals figure is not unusual but he is ahead by 1.87 when he was up 3.15 across the whole of last season. This trio are unlikely to maintain such hot form across another 30 league games.

Adding in João Pedro gives Chelsea four of the 12 players who are above their non-penalty xG by at least 1.5 in the Premier League this season. The two league games the Brazilian missed are the two in which Chelsea failed to score, mustering a combined 1.3 expected goals across those matches (against Brentford and Tottenham). João Pedro’s return from injury cannot come soon enough for the club.

This is not least because he provides a good focal point for the frontline, even when he is not scoring. Data from Gradient Sports shows João Pedro has had possession in the opposition penalty area 5.7 times per 90 minutes this season, the most among centre-forwards with at least 400 minutes in the Premier League. Despite playing in wide areas, Estêvão Willian’s average for this metric is 5.8 since joining Chelsea. No single stat can justify a player’s inclusion but the teenager is being omitted when he offers something the team lack in João Pedro’s absence.

Keeping possession in the penalty area has become increasingly difficult for Chelsea, who have dwindled after a positive start. Third in the division for opposition box touches after four matches, they now sit eighth. While Premier League home teams are averaging 27 touches per match in the box, Chelsea had 17 in their previous two games at Stamford Bridge. Given their possession average is markedly lower than in any recent campaign, it could prove difficult to increase their penalty area activity.

Alonso has overseen three league matches in which Chelsea had a maximum 38% possession; he had four such games in almost three years at Leverkusen. This is not as game-state driven as you might assume. Chelsea had 40.8% possession at the point they went 3-1 up at Fulham, 34.6% thereafter. They raced into a 3-0 lead against Brighton despite attempting 28.4% of the total passes to that point.

This cannot be by design when Alonso’s Bundesliga-winning Leverkusen team topped the German possession standings with 61.8%. He acknowledged as much when quizzed on the issue before Wednesday’s Carabao Cup defeat at Anfield. “You want to have possession,” Alonso said . “Knowing the context, knowing what we are building, I think that we have room for improvement in that part. We need to play more confidently with the ball.”

History shows Champions League qualification is unlikely with Chelsea’s 46.5% possession. The miracle of Leicester’s title win provides the only instance from the past 12 seasons of a team finishing in the top four with a lower possession average. Beyond that, West Ham finishing sixth in 2020-21 is the best showing.

Things may improve once the tactical plan becomes embedded and the lineup settles. Alonso has deployed 3-4-3 and 4-2-3-1, neither for more than three consecutive league games. Only Tottenham have averaged more changes to their starting XI from game to game in the Premier League (and this with neither side having to rotate owing to European commitments). Chelsea have started three goalkeepers, summoning distant memories of 1996-97 when Craig Forrest, Kevin Hitchcock, Nick Colgan, Frode Grodås and Dmitri Kharine got starts between the sticks. It is little surprise the Blues have the second-worst rate in the division for conceding over their expected goal level.

Much is up in the air at Stamford Bridge, yet there is a weird sense of certainty about Manchester United. They are a poor team and Carrick will surely leave soon. Alonso is a long way from the exit door but many questions need answering about his side.

title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you
text:
The US Federal Reserve has held interest rates steady at 3.75% - 4%.

The decision comes within a week of the midterm elections and after the central bank raised interest rates for the first time in three years at its September meeting.

"The overwhelming consensus, the overwhelming judgement, is that what we've done in this monetary medicine is starting to work some," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said, referring to September's interest rate rise.

Figures published after the Fed's announcement showed the US economy growing at a stronger pace than expected, with inflation running above the Fed's target.

An interest rate tells people and businesses how much it costs to borrow money – such as with credit cards, mortgages, or business loans – but also what return they get for saving cash.

The Fed influences interest rates in the US through its target range for the federal funds rate, which is the interest rate used by commercial banks for overnight borrowing.

In its decision to hold rates steady this month, the Fed said that while inflation remains high, it wanted to gather more information before making another decision to change rates.

The Fed also noted that while there was uncertainty, the US economy remained resilient.

Warsh acknowledged that inflation remained too high, but noted that there were other signs - such as tightening credit conditions - that the economy was moving in the right direction.

There is plenty more economic data to come between now and the committee's next meeting, the Fed chair added, which should paint a more detailed picture of the state of the economy.

At that point, Warsh said, "we'll be, I think, better positioned to determine the right policy decision and the stance of policy."

While last month the committee signalled there could be one more rate rise this year, Warsh would not be drawn out on where he thinks they will go in six weeks' time.

"A lot of things can happen, so I'm not going to be able to share with you my musings."

The decision to hold rates steady was not unanimous.

While 10 of the 12 committee members voted to keep rates unchanged, Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack voted to increase rates to 4%-4.25%, from its current 3.75%-4%.

The bank's next meeting will be held over 8-9 December.

Warsh said things are moving in the right direction, while the US economy is performing very strongly.

The US economy grew by 3.4% on an annualised basis in the three months to September, stronger than analysts had expected.

That strong growth was driven by an acceleration in investment, and strong consumer spending.

While there was an annualised increase in personal spending of 3.8%, the annualised increase in private investment was a huge 19.4% which analysts say was largely due to investment in artificial intelligence.

Inflation is also above the Fed's target range.

Prices increased by 3.7% in the year to September, driven higher by fuel and energy prices which have surged off the back of the war in Iran.

The Fed uses interest rate changes to try to keep inflation – the rate at which prices change – at 2% a year and keep the job market stable.

When inflation is too high, the Fed tends to raise interest rates.

This tends to mean higher rates from banks and other lenders, which in turn affects spending and saving decisions.

For example, someone refinancing their mortgage or buying a property for the first time could face higher mortgage rates. It could also mean higher interest rates on credit cards or car loans. However, it means higher interest rates on savings as well.

This encourages people and businesses to save more, spend less money, and make less investments. It also encourages companies to hire less people or slow the pace of pay rises.

All of this tends to reduce demand and slow inflation.

When inflation is low or if the Fed believes the economy needs a boost, it cut rates.

The idea is that this will have the opposite affect, with banks dropping rates leading to more spending and less saving from people and businesses.

Leaving the rates unchanged means rates on things like new mortgages or business loans are also less likely to change. It also means interest rates on cash savings are unlikely to rise.

US interest rates have historically moved around quite a bit.

The last time Fed rates were as high as they have been recently was in the lead up to and during the start of the 2008 global financial crisis.

The Fed then dropped rates to historic lows to encourage spending and job creation during the economic slump and kept them at those lows for several years.

They picked up again ahead of the pandemic before dropping to as low as 0%-0.25% during the pandemic. They then rose to highs of 5.25%-5% from the middle of 2023 to August 2024 as inflation jumped.

They had been falling steadily since then, until rates were raised last month.

author: Antonio Losada
text:
It’s not even Halloween, the NBA season is barely a week old, but the injury report already looks like something you’d expect to read in April.

Here in Mexico City, I can relate. You can feel in the air, both figuratively and literally. We’re just days — hours, if you push it — away from one of the biggest festivities in the country to take place this weekend.
